paragraphs.text: Zelensky hardened his tone towards Washington. In BBC interviews published on 26–27 Nov he said “The United States cannot simply be a mediator, a neutral one”, called Putin “an aggressor and a killer” in reply to Trump’s “friend” remark at Shenzhen, and pointed to a severe shortage of Patriot and anti-ballistic interceptors as the US prioritises the Middle East. Patriot transfers still await sign-off by Secretary of War Hegseth, and Starshield restrictions continue to hamper UKR interceptions of jet-powered drones.

UKR is widening its strike campaign beyond its own theatre. After a Stavka meeting on 27 Nov, Zelensky said the long-range strike plan had been adjusted to slow RUS military production and that operations “in neutral waters” would be coordinated with partners. The coordination claim is contested: ITA FM Tajani said on 27 Nov that Zelensky’s statement on coordinating the 22 Nov naval-drone strike on the RUS corvette Merkury at Benghazi was “not true”, after PM Meloni warned the war must not reach the Mediterranean. European unease over escalation at sea is likely to grow.

Pressure on LVA is rising on two fronts. RUS MFA spokeswoman Zakharova said on 27 Nov that Riga “stands at the forefront of confrontation with Russia”, that Moscow reserves the right to “decisive retaliatory measures” over the Kulbergs government’s planned declaration on “derussification”, and that LVA would not normalise relations even after a ceasefire. Overnight on 26–27 Nov a UAV briefly entered LVA airspace near Ludza; NATO Baltic Air Policing fighters were scrambled and an interceptor drone launched. The origin was not identified; EST issued a similar air-threat alert in six southern counties the same morning, amid UKR drone strikes on the Leningrad region.

The EU’s €45 billion instrument for UKR in 2027 remains open after the special European Council of 26–27 Nov deferred the decision to December. President Costa said 24 member states back it, with BGR limiting its participation to the non-military component, while SVK, HUN and CZE hold out; Chancellor Merz has threatened to halt talks on the long-term budget unless all contribute. Next step: the European Council on 17–18 Dec.

Zelensky said important meetings on security guarantees are expected in UKR next week and noted progress on prisoner exchanges and on European representation in the talks. No date, venue or list of participants has been announced, and there is no public RUS reply on the guarantees.

ISW assessed on 27 Nov that Moscow “may be preparing a false flag operation” against MDA, after the RUS Embassy in Chisinau warned on 26 Nov of a possible “provocation”. MDA, bordering ROU, has seen repeated RUS drone incursions this autumn. ISW also links the arrest of RUS Aerospace Forces deputy commander Col. Grekhov to possible scapegoating for air defence failures.

NATO responded to the 20 Nov RUS missile incursion into POL with an extraordinary NAC on 23 Nov: allies said Russia “bears full responsibility” and SACEUR forward-deployed one AWACS; POL did not invoke Article 4. A RUS jet-powered drone then flew ~20 km into POL airspace for nine minutes, which the MoD judges deliberate. On 25 Nov Warsaw went further: it has asked allies to consider intercepting RUS missiles over UKR heading for NATO territory, which FM Sikorski calls self-defence if done at Kyiv’s request, but there is no consensus and Deputy MoD Tomczyk said NATO is not supportive. POL will instead create a no-fly zone extending over 10 km from the UKR border by late Dec/early Jan, and Sikorski said expelling the RUS ambassador is under consideration, with no immediate plan.

The special European Council on 26–27 Nov ended without agreement after almost 14 hours. The €45 billion instrument for UKR in 2027 (€20 billion budget support, €25 billion military) was not supported by SVK, HUN and CZE, and BGR will join only the civilian part; the 2028–2034 budget talks also stalled. Costa said leaders “will revert to this issue in December”, i.e. at the 17–18 Dec European Council, while Macron warned that abandoning UKR “would jeopardise our own security”. Peskov called the EU funding “not money for peace”. Kyiv’s 2027 financing gap therefore remains open for at least three more weeks.

Rutte met Trump at Mar-a-Lago on 25 Nov. Their joint statement, published by NATO on 26 Nov, called the meeting “outstanding”, urged RUS to avoid actions that “intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war” and stressed higher defence spending and production across NATO; it also covered Iran. The next day Trump posted that he wants Putin to “pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe”; Peskov replied that the call appears aimed at Kyiv. No new US commitment on UKR was announced, and Hegseth is expected to announce the review of US force presence in Europe in the coming weeks.

RUS sabotage pressure on European supporters of UKR is rising. MI5’s National Protective Security Authority and the MoD warned UK firms supplying UKR’s armed forces on 24–25 Nov that RUS proxies may target them, typically by arson. On 26 Nov MFA spokeswoman Zakharova said civilian staff of Western defence firms involved in UKR strikes are “not only legitimate military targets” but face criminal liability, naming Destinus. An IISS report released the same day finds that sabotage with explosives and arson roughly doubled over the past year, with GER and POL accounting for over half of incidents and a growing risk of mass casualties; arrests and expulsions have not deterred Moscow.

The Bundestag adopted the 2027 defence budget on 25 Nov (CDU/CSU and SPD for; AfD, Greens and Left against): €139.4 billion in total, including €29.6 billion from the Bundeswehr special fund, with procurement above €60 billion. In the general debate the same day Merz said Russia “wants more than Ukraine” and is escalating “massively” in GER too, while AfD leader Chrupalla attacked Ukraine aid. On 23 Nov Pistorius hosted UKR Defence Minister Khmara, funding ~€34 million of production capacity for the Babka reconnaissance drone and signing an MoI on the Delta battle-management system.

UKR air defence remains the pressing gap. Zelensky said on 25 Nov that partners committed more than $700 million under PURL after Ramstein, specifically for anti-ballistic interceptors, and that NOR and GER took new decisions on air defence and interceptor production, but US Patriot deliveries are “still delayed”; ISW counts at least 48 PURL-funded Patriot interceptors held up. On 26 Nov he warned of another massive RUS strike being prepared and said new weapons packages from partners “in Europe and beyond” are being worked out to protect infrastructure against drones.

Zelensky confirmed the 21 Nov UKR strike on the cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, which he said carried weapons and drifted into FIN waters after being hit in RUS waters. Acknowledging that “some European partners are worried” about Baltic incidents, he ordered officials to brief partners in advance. LTU rejected RUS claims that a drone targeting Kaliningrad came from its territory.

At the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin, Rutte urged national parliaments to vote the budgets needed for the new spending commitments; the Assembly called for a shift from short-term aid to a defence-industrial partnership with UKR. Wadephul said “Protecting Vilnius is protecting Berlin”, while Merz called reports of a RUS nuclear-capable satellite shocking; Peskov said they were “hardly worth taking seriously”.

The fight is now over the format of the next round. Zelensky said on 25 Nov that Kyiv is “waiting for the American side to set a date” for a meeting that should now be quadrilateral (UKR, US, Europe, RUS), and von der Leyen announced that a strong European team will join. Moscow is resisting: Peskov saw no “added value” in Europeans on 24 Nov, and DFM Ryabkov said on 25 Nov that the E3 are invited to Moscow but would “lose any chance of taking part” if they set preconditions. On 26 Nov Peskov said the process “isn’t going along smoothly” and dismissed the EU’s claim to a mediating role; only a prisoner exchange under the Abu Dhabi arrangements is being prepared. No date or venue has been set since the Abu Dhabi round of 10–11 Nov.

US envoy Kushner, in a podcast with Axel Springer’s Döpfner released on 25 Nov, said the war has “effectively become a proxy war” funded by Europe, that territorial talks are deadlocked and that Putin is not interested in a ceasefire-first approach. In another podcast reported on 26 Nov he said Putin “has showed restraint” and agreed not to use nuclear weapons. The framing sits uneasily with Washington’s role as broker and will be welcome in Moscow. ISW judges that the approval chain for the Article 5-like guarantees in the US plan “may well prove impossible to execute”.

FIN, SWE, NOR, LTU and NLD will jointly procure more than 430 CV90 infantry fighting vehicles from BAE Systems Hägglunds, with SWE as lead nation; FIN takes 160 for €2.835 billion. Finnish MoD Häkkänen called it NATO’s largest joint land procurement; the vehicles are expected to include counter-drone capability. EST signed the 2025 statement of intent but withdrew.

HUN PM Péter Magyar met Zelensky in Zakarpattia on 24 Nov, a marked change of tone in bilateral relations. They agreed on cooperation on energy (diesel supplies to UKR), rail links and border crossings, and UKR offered corn after Hungary’s poor harvest; Zelensky welcomed HUN support for opening UKR’s EU accession clusters and said “Friendship with Putin leads nowhere”.

ROU issued an RO-Alert in northern Tulcea on 24 Nov after radar detected a presumed RUS drone in UKR airspace near the border; two ESP F-18s on NATO air policing scrambled from Mihail Kogălniceanu. MApN reported no violation of ROU airspace.
